Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: After the assassination of Muhammad Ghori in March 1206, Aibak fought with another former slave-general Taj al-Din Yildiz for control of Ghurid territories in north-western India.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: During this campaign, he advanced as far as _____, although he later retreated and set up his capital at Lahore
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: During this campaign, he advanced as far as Ghazni, although he later retreated and set up his capital at Lahore.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: He nominally acknowledged the suzerainty of _____'s successor Ghiyasuddin Mahmud, who officially recognized him as the ruler of India
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: After the assassination of Muhammad Ghori in March 1206, Aibak fought with another former slave-general Taj al-Din Yildiz for control of Ghurid territories in north-western India. He nominally acknowledged the suzerainty of Muhammad Ghori's successor Ghiyasuddin Mahmud, who officially recognized him as the ruler of India.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Aibak was succeeded by _____, and then by his former slave and son-in-law Iltutmish, who transformed the loosely-held Ghurid territories of India into the powerful Delhi Sultanate
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Aibak was succeeded by Aram Shah, and then by his former slave and son-in-law Iltutmish, who transformed the loosely-held Ghurid territories of India into the powerful Delhi Sultanate.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Aibak is known for having commissioned the _____ in Delhi, and the Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra in Ajmer
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Aibak is known for having commissioned the Qutb Minar in Delhi, and the Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra in Ajmer.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: His name is variously transliterated as "Qutb al-_____", "Qutbuddin Aibek", and "Kutb Al-Din Aybak"
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: His name is variously transliterated as "Qutb al-Din Aybeg", "Qutbuddin Aibek", and "Kutb Al-Din Aybak".

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: He came from _____, and belonged to a Turkic tribe called Aibak
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: He came from Turkestan, and belonged to a Turkic tribe called Aibak.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: The word "Aibak", also transliterated as "Aibek" or "Aybeg", derives from the _____ words for "moon" (ai) and "lord" (bek)
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: He came from Turkestan, and belonged to a Turkic tribe called Aibak. The word "Aibak", also transliterated as "Aibek" or "Aybeg", derives from the Turkic words for "moon" (ai) and "lord" (bek).

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: As a child, he was separated from his family and taken to the slave market of _____
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: As a child, he was separated from his family and taken to the slave market of Nishapur.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: There, _____, a descendant of the noted Muslim theologian Abu Hanifa, purchased him
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: There, Qazi Fakhruddin Abdul Aziz Kufi, a descendant of the noted Muslim theologian Abu Hanifa, purchased him.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Aibak was treated affectionately in the _____'s household and was educated with the Qazi's sons
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: There, Qazi Fakhruddin Abdul Aziz Kufi, a descendant of the noted Muslim theologian Abu Hanifa, purchased him. Aibak was treated affectionately in the Qazi's household and was educated with the Qazi's sons.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: He learned archery and horse-riding, besides _____ recital
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Qutb ud-Din Aibak (Persian: قطب‌الدین ایبک; 1150 – 4 November 1210) was a Turkic general of the Ghurid emperor Muhammad Ghori. He was in charge of the Ghurid territories in northern India, and after Muhammad Ghori's assassination in 1206, he set up his own independent rule in Lahore, and laid the foundations for the Sultanate of Delhi.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: The Qazi or one of his sons sold Aibak to a merchant, who in turn, sold the boy to the _____ in Ghazni
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: The Qazi or one of his sons sold Aibak to a merchant, who in turn, sold the boy to the Ghurid Sultan Muhammad Ghori in Ghazni.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: After being admitted to the _____'s slave-household, Aibak's intelligence and kind nature attracted the Sultan's attention
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: The Qazi or one of his sons sold Aibak to a merchant, who in turn, sold the boy to the Ghurid Sultan Muhammad Ghori in Ghazni. After being admitted to the Sultan's slave-household, Aibak's intelligence and kind nature attracted the Sultan's attention.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Once, when the _____ bestowed gifts upon his slaves, Aibak distributed his share among the servants
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: The Qazi or one of his sons sold Aibak to a merchant, who in turn, sold the boy to the Ghurid Sultan Muhammad Ghori in Ghazni. After being admitted to the Sultan's slave-household, Aibak's intelligence and kind nature attracted the Sultan's attention.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Impressed by this act, the _____ promoted him to a higher rank
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: The Qazi or one of his sons sold Aibak to a merchant, who in turn, sold the boy to the Ghurid Sultan Muhammad Ghori in Ghazni. After being admitted to the Sultan's slave-household, Aibak's intelligence and kind nature attracted the Sultan's attention.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Aibak later rose to the important position of _____-i Akhur, the officer of the royal stables
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Aibak later rose to the important position of Amir-i Akhur, the officer of the royal stables.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: During the _____ conflicts with the Khwarazmian ruler Sultan Shah, Aibak was responsible for the general maintenance of the horses, as well as their fodder and equipment
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: During the Ghurid conflicts with the Khwarazmian ruler Sultan Shah, Aibak was responsible for the general maintenance of the horses, as well as their fodder and equipment. After the Ghurids defeated Sultan Shah, Muhammad Ghori ad-Din saw him in the cage and was deeply touched by his desperate condition.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: One day, while foraging for horse fodder, he was captured by _____'s scouts and was detained in an iron cage
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: During the Ghurid conflicts with the Khwarazmian ruler Sultan Shah, Aibak was responsible for the general maintenance of the horses, as well as their fodder and equipment. One day, while foraging for horse fodder, he was captured by Sultan Shah's scouts and was detained in an iron cage.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: After the Ghurids defeated _____, Muhammad Ghori ad-Din saw him in the cage and was deeply touched by his desperate condition
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: During the Ghurid conflicts with the Khwarazmian ruler Sultan Shah, Aibak was responsible for the general maintenance of the horses, as well as their fodder and equipment. One day, while foraging for horse fodder, he was captured by Sultan Shah's scouts and was detained in an iron cage.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: After he was released, the _____ greatly favoured him
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: During the Ghurid conflicts with the Khwarazmian ruler Sultan Shah, Aibak was responsible for the general maintenance of the horses, as well as their fodder and equipment. One day, while foraging for horse fodder, he was captured by Sultan Shah's scouts and was detained in an iron cage.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: No information is available about Aibak's subsequent assignments until the First Battle of Tarain fought in India, in _____–1192
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: No information is available about Aibak's subsequent assignments until the First Battle of Tarain fought in India, in 1191–1192.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: No information is available about Aibak's subsequent assignments until the _____ of Tarain fought in India, in 1191–1192
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: No information is available about Aibak's subsequent assignments until the First Battle of Tarain fought in India, in 1191–1192.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: After his victory at Tarain, _____ assigned the former Chahamana territory to Aibak, who was placed at Kuhram (present-day Ghuram in Punjab, India)
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: At the Second Battle of Tarain, where the Ghurids emerged victorious, he was in charge of the general disposition of the Ghurid army and kept close to Sultan Muhammad Ghori, who had placed himself at the centre of the army. After his victory at Tarain, Muhammad Ghori assigned the former Chahamana territory to Aibak, who was placed at Kuhram (present-day Ghuram in Punjab, India).

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: After the death of _____, Aibak appointed his son Govindaraja IV as a Ghurid vassal
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: After the death of Prithviraja, Aibak appointed his son Govindaraja IV as a Ghurid vassal. Sometime later, Prithviraja's brother Hariraja invaded the Ranthambore Fort, which Aibak had placed under his subordinate Qawamul Mulk.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Sometime later, _____'s brother Hariraja invaded the Ranthambore Fort, which Aibak had placed under his subordinate Qawamul Mulk
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: After the death of Prithviraja, Aibak appointed his son Govindaraja IV as a Ghurid vassal. Sometime later, Prithviraja's brother Hariraja invaded the Ranthambore Fort, which Aibak had placed under his subordinate Qawamul Mulk.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Aibak marched to _____, forcing Hariraja to retreat from Ranthambore as well as the former Chahamana capital Ajmer
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Sometime later, Prithviraja's brother Hariraja invaded the Ranthambore Fort, which Aibak had placed under his subordinate Qawamul Mulk. Aibak marched to Ranthambore, forcing Hariraja to retreat from Ranthambore as well as the former Chahamana capital Ajmer.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Aibak marched to Hansi, forcing _____ to retreat to Bagar, where the rebel was defeated and killed in a battle
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Aibak marched to Hansi, forcing Jatwan to retreat to Bagar, where the rebel was defeated and killed in a battle. The above-mentioned information about Jatwan's rebellion comes from the contemporary writer Hasan Nizami.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: The above-mentioned information about Jatwan's rebellion comes from the contemporary writer _____
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: The above-mentioned information about Jatwan's rebellion comes from the contemporary writer Hasan Nizami.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Firishta (17th century), however, dates the rebellion to _____, and states that Jatwan retreated to the frontiers of Gujarat after his defeat
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Firishta (17th century), however, dates the rebellion to 1203, and states that Jatwan retreated to the frontiers of Gujarat after his defeat.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: He was later killed as a subordinate of the _____ king Bhima II when Aibak invaded Gujarat
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: He was later killed as a subordinate of the Chaulukya king Bhima II when Aibak invaded Gujarat. Historian A.K. Majumdar adds that Firishta may have confused the Chaulukya ruler Bhima with Bhima-simha, who - according to the Kharatara Gaccha Pattavali - was the governor of Hansi in 1171 CE.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: According to historian _____, Firishta may have confused the Bagar tract (where Jatwan was killed) with another area called Bagar near the Gujarat border, around Banswara and Dungarpur
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: According to historian Dasharatha Sharma, Firishta may have confused the Bagar tract (where Jatwan was killed) with another area called Bagar near the Gujarat border, around Banswara and Dungarpur.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Historian A.K. Majumdar adds that Firishta may have confused the Chaulukya ruler Bhima with Bhima-simha, who - according to the Kharatara Gaccha Pattavali - was the governor of Hansi in _____ CE
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Historian A.K. Majumdar adds that Firishta may have confused the Chaulukya ruler Bhima with Bhima-simha, who - according to the Kharatara Gaccha Pattavali - was the governor of Hansi in 1171 CE.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Thus, _____ may have been a general of Bhima-simha, and may have tried to recover the fort on behalf of his master
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: According to historian Dasharatha Sharma, Firishta may have confused the Bagar tract (where Jatwan was killed) with another area called Bagar near the Gujarat border, around Banswara and Dungarpur. Thus, Jatwan may have been a general of Bhima-simha, and may have tried to recover the fort on behalf of his master.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Nizami does not state this, and _____'s guess appears to be based on the similarity of the words "Jatwan" and "Jat", and the rebellion's locality, where Jats can be found
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Nizami does not state this, and Elliot's guess appears to be based on the similarity of the words "Jatwan" and "Jat", and the rebellion's locality, where Jats can be found.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: According to S.H. _____, "Jatwan" is a mistranscription of the "Chahwan" in the manuscript, and the rebel was probably a Chahamana (Chawhan or Chauhan) subordinate of Prithivraja
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: According to S.H. Hodivala, "Jatwan" is a mistranscription of the "Chahwan" in the manuscript, and the rebel was probably a Chahamana (Chawhan or Chauhan) subordinate of Prithivraja.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: According to _____, it is probably a corrupt form of the name "Jaitra"
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: According to Rima Hooja, it is probably a corrupt form of the name "Jaitra".

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: In _____, he took control of Meerut and Baran (modern Bulandshahr), from where he would later launch attacks against the Gahadavala kingdom
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: In 1192, he took control of Meerut and Baran (modern Bulandshahr), from where he would later launch attacks against the Gahadavala kingdom. He also took control of Delhi in 1192, where he initially retained the local Tomara ruler as a vassal.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: He also took control of Delhi in _____, where he initially retained the local Tomara ruler as a vassal
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: In 1192, he took control of Meerut and Baran (modern Bulandshahr), from where he would later launch attacks against the Gahadavala kingdom. He also took control of Delhi in 1192, where he initially retained the local Tomara ruler as a vassal.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: In _____, he deposed the Tomara ruler for treason and took direct control of Delhi
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: In 1193, he deposed the Tomara ruler for treason and took direct control of Delhi.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: The near-contemporary chronicler _____ does not elaborate why, but the 14th-century chronicler Isami claims that some people had aroused the Sultan's suspicion about Aibak's loyalty
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: The near-contemporary chronicler Minhaj does not elaborate why, but the 14th-century chronicler Isami claims that some people had aroused the Sultan's suspicion about Aibak's loyalty.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Historian K. A. Nizami finds Isami's account unreliable and theorizes that the _____ may have sought Aibak's help in planning further Ghurid expansion in India
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: The near-contemporary chronicler Minhaj does not elaborate why, but the 14th-century chronicler Isami claims that some people had aroused the Sultan's suspicion about Aibak's loyalty. Historian K. A. Nizami finds Isami's account unreliable and theorizes that the Sultan may have sought Aibak's help in planning further Ghurid expansion in India.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: After his return to India in _____, he crossed the Yamuna River, and captured Koil (modern Aligarh) from the Dor Rajputs
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: After his return to India in 1194, he crossed the Yamuna River, and captured Koil (modern Aligarh) from the Dor Rajputs.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: After his return to India in 1194, he crossed the _____, and captured Koil (modern Aligarh) from the Dor Rajputs
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: After his return to India in 1194, he crossed the Yamuna River, and captured Koil (modern Aligarh) from the Dor Rajputs.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Meanwhile, taking advantage of Aibak's absence in India, _____ had regained control of a part of the former Chahamana territory
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Meanwhile, taking advantage of Aibak's absence in India, Hariraja had regained control of a part of the former Chahamana territory. After his return to Delhi, Aibak sent an army against Hariraja, who committed suicide when faced with certain defeat.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: After his return to Delhi, Aibak sent an army against _____, who committed suicide when faced with certain defeat
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Meanwhile, taking advantage of Aibak's absence in India, Hariraja had regained control of a part of the former Chahamana territory. After his return to Delhi, Aibak sent an army against Hariraja, who committed suicide when faced with certain defeat.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Aibak subsequently placed Ajmer under a Muslim governor and moved _____ to Ranthambore
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Aibak subsequently placed Ajmer under a Muslim governor and moved Govindaraja to Ranthambore.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: After the battle, _____ continued his advance to the east, with Aibek in the vanguard
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: After the battle, Muhammad Ghori continued his advance to the east, with Aibek in the vanguard.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Although the _____ did not gain complete control over the Gahadavala kingdom, the victory provided an opportunity for them to establish military stations at many places in the region
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Although the Ghurids did not gain complete control over the Gahadavala kingdom, the victory provided an opportunity for them to establish military stations at many places in the region.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Muhammad Ghori returned to Ghazni but came back to India in _____–96 when he defeated Kumarapala, the Bhati ruler of Bayana
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Muhammad Ghori returned to Ghazni but came back to India in 1195–96 when he defeated Kumarapala, the Bhati ruler of Bayana.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: He then marched towards _____, where the local Parihara ruler Sallakhanapala acknowledged his suzerainty after a long siege
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: He then marched towards Gwalior, where the local Parihara ruler Sallakhanapala acknowledged his suzerainty after a long siege.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Meanwhile, the Mher tribals, who lived near Ajmer, rebelled against the _____ rule
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Although the Ghurids did not gain complete control over the Gahadavala kingdom, the victory provided an opportunity for them to establish military stations at many places in the region. Meanwhile, the Mher tribals, who lived near Ajmer, rebelled against the Ghurid rule.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Supported by the _____, who ruled Gujarat in the south, the Mhers posed a serious threat to Aibak's control of the region
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Supported by the Chaulukyas, who ruled Gujarat in the south, the Mhers posed a serious threat to Aibak's control of the region.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Aibak marched against them but was forced to retreat to _____
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Meanwhile, the Mher tribals, who lived near Ajmer, rebelled against the Ghurid rule. Aibak marched against them but was forced to retreat to Ajmer.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: The Mhers were forced to retreat after reinforcements from the _____ capital of Ghazni arrived in Ajmer
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Meanwhile, the Mher tribals, who lived near Ajmer, rebelled against the Ghurid rule. The Mhers were forced to retreat after reinforcements from the Ghurid capital of Ghazni arrived in Ajmer.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: In _____, Aibak defeated the Chaulukya army at Mount Abu, thus avenging Muhammad Ghori's defeat at the Battle of Kasahrada nearly two decades earlier
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: In 1197, Aibak defeated the Chaulukya army at Mount Abu, thus avenging Muhammad Ghori's defeat at the Battle of Kasahrada nearly two decades earlier.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Aibak's army then marched to the _____ capital Anhilwara: the defending king Bhima II fled the city, which was plundered by the invaders
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: In 1197, Aibak defeated the Chaulukya army at Mount Abu, thus avenging Muhammad Ghori's defeat at the Battle of Kasahrada nearly two decades earlier. Aibak's army then marched to the Chaulukya capital Anhilwara: the defending king Bhima II fled the city, which was plundered by the invaders.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Minhaj characterizes Aibak's raid of _____ as the "conquest of Gujarat", but it did not result in the annexation of Gujarat to the Ghurid Empire
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Aibak's army then marched to the Chaulukya capital Anhilwara: the defending king Bhima II fled the city, which was plundered by the invaders. Minhaj characterizes Aibak's raid of Anhilwara as the "conquest of Gujarat", but it did not result in the annexation of Gujarat to the Ghurid Empire.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Whatever the case, _____ control of the region did not last long, and the Chaulukyas regained control of their capital soon after
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Minhaj characterizes Aibak's raid of Anhilwara as the "conquest of Gujarat", but it did not result in the annexation of Gujarat to the Ghurid Empire. The 16th-century historian Firishta states that Aibak appointed a Muslim officer to consolidate Ghurid power in the region, while Ibn-i Asir states that Aibak placed the newly-captured territory under Hindu vassals.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: In _____–98, Aibak conquered Budaun in present-day Uttar Pradesh, and also re-took control of the former Gahadavala capital Varanasi, which had slipped out of Ghurid control
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: In 1197–98, Aibak conquered Budaun in present-day Uttar Pradesh, and also re-took control of the former Gahadavala capital Varanasi, which had slipped out of Ghurid control.
